title: First Thing: Pope Leo recovering from surgery after lung cancer diagnosis
summary:
Vatican says operation on US-born head of Roman Catholic church was ‘successful’. Plus, after six decades in the US, Joni Mitchell has become a citizen

Good morning. Pope Leo XIV, the head…

blocks.text: Good morning. Pope Leo XIV, the head of the 1.4 billion-strong Roman Catholic church, has been diagnosed with lung cancer. The Vatican made the announcement after Leo, 71, the first US-born leader to assume the role, underwent an operation and had the lower lobe of his right lung removed. A statement said the surgery was “successful, on schedule and as planned”.

The Vatican said Leo had “now returned to his room” after the operation. All of his appointments have been cancelled until 20 October. The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, a practising Catholic who has met the pope, said he and his wife were “united in prayers” for Leo after the diagnosis.

blocks.caption: Trump and the press pack at the White House. Photograph: Samuel Corum/EPA

blocks.text: Donald Trump faced another setback in his battle over media coverage after a federal judge ordered that journalists from CNN, MS Now and Politico must still have access to the White House as the media coalition’s lawsuit against the administration plays out.

In his ruling on Tuesday, Judge Kelly wrote that the plaintiffs “are likely to succeed not only on their due process claim, but also on their two first amendment claims”. While access to the White House is not guaranteed, court precedent dictates that once it is provided to journalists, it cannot be taken away for editorial or viewpoint-based reasons.

items: What is the latest in Trump’s legal battle with the BBC? The BBC is asking a federal judge in Florida to force Donald Trump to sit for a deposition as part of the president’s $10bn defamation lawsuit against the British broadcaster. The president has so far declined to set a date to appear. “Plaintiff chose to file this lawsuit and, in doing so, he accepted the obligations of civil litigation,” the BBC’s motion reads. “The BBC therefore asks the court to compel plaintiff to confirm a date.”

blocks.text: Kimberly Guilfoyle ousted as US ambassador to Greece

blocks.caption: Kimberly Guilfoyle speaks as Donald Trump watches on. Photograph: Jacquelyn Martin/AP

blocks.text: Kimberly Guilfoyle is stepping down as US ambassador to Greece after weeks of reports that she sought payment from a Donald Trump donor in exchange for access to administration officials. The decision ends the diplomatic career of one of the US president’s longest-standing political allies.

The former fiancee of Donald Trump Jr, Guilfoyle confirmed her departure from the post which she described as the “honor of a lifetime”. She said she would “vigorously defend my name, my reputation and my integrity” and that “my commitment to President Trump, the America First movement, and the country I love will never end”.

items: What were the allegations against Guilfoyle? The Wall Street Journal reported she used Signal messages to press the donor Eric Deters to pay a $100,000 credit card bill in exchange for official influence – a request Deters described as a quid pro quo. She was also accused of accepting improper gifts and promoting a private Greek firm during official business. Guilfoyle strongly contests all allegations and disputes the authenticity of the messages.

blocks.text: Cornell suspends fraternity parties amid backlash over alleged sexual assault

blocks.caption: Students protest at Cornell University. Photograph: Olga Fedorova/EPA

blocks.text: Cornell University has announced it is suspending parties and other social gatherings at fraternity houses for the rest of the academic year amid intensifying backlash over its handling of allegations that a female student was sexually assaulted at a fraternity house in 2024. The university has also said it will involve New York state police in investigating alleged sex crimes on campus.
Duane ‘Keffe D’ Davis sentenced to 40 years to life over Tupac Shakur’s murder

blocks.caption: Duane ‘Keffe D’ Davis in court. Photograph: Steve Marcus/Reuters

blocks.text: Duane “Keffe D” Davis, the former California gang leader convicted of murder for orchestrating the 1996 fatal shooting of the rapper Tupac Shakur, has been sentenced to 40 years to life in prison. Judge Carli Kierny said as she delivered the sentence: “You don’t get to take a man from his family. You don’t get to take his very life, his whole future from him and just walk away from it.” On 7 September 1996, Shakur was gunned down near the Las Vegas strip shortly after a Mike Tyson boxing match. He succumbed to his injuries days later.
In other news …

blocks.caption: The aftermath of Hurricane Isaias. Photograph: Gerald Herbert/AP

items: Six deaths have been confirmed in Florida in the aftermath of Hurricane Isaias. The state’s governor praised Floridians and local officials for taking proper precautions, linking it to there being a lower death toll compared with previous storms.
A sixth death has been announced in Pennsylvania’s measles outbreak, as new figures show cases in the state have risen above 1,100.

An Iranian woman has been handed a death sentence for “blasphemy” in a social media post, as rights groups warn of Tehran’s increasing use of executions to suppress dissent, with at least 600 this year.
Apple has unveiled new smart home devices that showcase an upgraded Siri AI. HomeView, an iPad-like device, acts as a hub for other smart home gadgets.
Lena Dunham’s Girls is returning for a limited run at HBO. The creator and star will return along with other key cast members for a five-episode revival.

blocks.text: Stat of the day: Elon Musk becomes biggest donor of US midterms cycle with $366m spent

blocks.caption: Elon Musk. Photograph: Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP

blocks.text: Musk’s midterm donations, mostly for rightwing candidates and causes, surpass his contributions to Trump in 2024. Meanwhile, Ukrainian soldiers in combat have suddenly had their access to Starlink satellite internet terminals restricted. Managed by Musk’s SpaceX, the terminals are a key component of Ukraine’s military operations, and the sudden restrictions led to the failure of several combat missions.
Well Actually: They’re delicious, popular and versatile – but how healthy are berries?

blocks.caption: A bowl of fresh berries. Photograph: Cavan Images/Alamy

blocks.text: Experts say that if you’re eating any berry – strawberries, blackberries, currants, raspberries, blueberries – you’re benefiting. “All berries are good. We should eat a heck of a lot more than we do,” says Mary Ann Lila, a professor in the department of food, bioprocessing, and nutrition sciences at North Carolina State University.

My colleague Vivian Ho has been looking to find out how realistic the promises of “passive income” schemes are, and whether she could actually make money from any of them. It’s a great read.
Climate check: Scientists deploy a 24-armed secret weapon to save California’s kelp forests

blocks.caption: A large group of sunflower sea stars. Photograph: Nature Picture Library/Alamy

blocks.text: Off the coast of Monterey, California, a team of researchers is working to restore the sunflower sea star, as 95% of these key underwater ecosystems along the Pacific coast have been decimated in past decade.
Last Thing: Joni Mitchell becomes US citizen

blocks.caption: Joni Mitchell at her US citizenship ceremony. Photograph: Instagram

blocks.text: Joni Mitchell has become a US citizen, after first moving to the country in the mid-1960s. The Canada-born singer-songwriter, 82, posted footage of her citizenship ceremony on her Instagram account, saying it was “a journey that began 62 years ago”.
